answer.diagnosis: Only 18 of the 32 layer-1 units look trained, and they form two opposite families. Large-blob units 3, 7, 8, 21, 22, 24, 27 and 28 have a positive annulus at roughly rows 5-18 and cols 5-18, and a slightly negative centre. Small-blob units 2, 4, 14, 17, 18, 19, 25, 26, 29 and 30 have a positive centre at rows 10-13 and cols 10-13, a negative surrounding ring, and broadly positive periphery weights. The positive periphery acts roughly like extra bias when the background is dark. The remaining units (0, 1, 5, 6, 9-13, 15, 16, 20, 23, 31) have small, unstructured weights of about ±25, consistent with untrained initial values. I searched for a localized spurious cue: a corner patch, a marker dot, a border frame, a stripe or checkerboard, or one unit dedicated to a patch. I found none. There are scattered strong peripheral pixels, for example (1,16), (1,17), (8,2), (3,12), (16,21), (20,19) and (0,4), (0,11), (23,11). These are shared across each family with opposite signs, but the pattern is salt-and-pepper: adjacent pixels often have opposite signs, such as (1,16)/(1,17) against (0,17). There is no contiguous, same-sign patch. This looks like per-pixel memorization of background noise, with magnitudes possibly inflated by an adaptive optimizer, rather than a coherent shortcut feature. The class logic is carried by the centre-versus-annulus size detectors, so I make no edits. Residual uncertainty: the dense peripheral texture could in principle be a fixed class-correlated background pattern, but the weights do not single out a separable feature that could be cleanly removed.
